hook: A Roman ghost story|that *ends* with bones

lines.say: Almost two thousand years ago, a Roman writer named Pliny the Younger wrote a letter asking a friend: do ghosts exist?
shots: archive: Pliny the Younger statue Como (public domain photo)
q: Roman letter wax tablet stylus

lines.say: Then he tells a story. In Athens there was a big house nobody would live in.
At night you'd hear chains. Then an old man would appear, thin, filthy, with chains on his legs and wrists, rattling them.
A philosopher named Athenodorus rented it anyway, because it was cheap. He sat up writing. The ghost came. It beckoned. He followed it into the courtyard, where it vanished.
shots: q: oil lamp writing desk night

lines.say: He marked the spot with leaves. The next day he had it dug up.
They found bones, tangled in chains. They gave them a proper burial. And the haunting stopped.
shots: q: old bones in soil archaeology

lines.say: The chained ghost, the unburied body, the haunting that ends with a burial. Ghost stories have barely changed since.
